Although the violence that flared up was in isolated areas, it got Khalef Kalifa from Muslims for Human Rights anxious.As an election observer he said police seemed "ill prepared" for any clashes and that in some polling stations computers were not working and "in one polling station a voter had to come and show the presiding offer how to use the computer." But election officials promised voters they would keep the polling stations open to compensate for earlier delays. By the time the evening call to prayer could bear heard echoing out from the mosques of Mombasa, Festus Mwanzia was number 27 in the queue. He had waited patiently in line for nearly 12 hours. "I'll be home by 10," he chirped confidently. "Just in time to catch the results on TV." Many people here know the biggest test is yet to come once the tallying gets under way. In the western town of Eldoret, the provincial capital of the Rift Valley where much of the post-election violence occurred following the December 2007 election, voting started early in the morning with enthusiastic voters arriving as early as 05:00. There were long queues, some stretching for a kilometre. At the MV Patel polling station which has the highest number of registered voters in the region, people complained that the process was too slow. In Shinyalu, in the rural Kakamega district - between Eldoret and Kisumu - the area's former member of parliament, Justus Kizito, was ambushed in the early hours of the morning and his Range Rover was burnt to ashes. He says the attack was political and forced to flee for fear of his life before the mob set the vehicle on fire. At Kosachei Primary School near Eldoret, William Ruto, a suspect at the International Criminal Court from the Kalenjin community and running mate to presidential candidate and fellow indictee Uhuru Kenyatta, a Kikuyu, cast his vote at 07:30. Afterwards he told me that should their Jubilee coalition win, they would co-operate with the ICC in the hope of clearing their names. The two, who were rivals during the last poll, both deny charges of orchestrating the violence following the 2007 vote. At the Kiambaa polling station - just a stone's throw from the ill-fated church where more than 40 Kikuyu people who had sought shelter there were burnt alive on 1 January 2008, when it was set ablaze by a mob of armed Kalenjin youth - most voters were happy to have cast their ballots in peace. Paty Chelegat, a Kalenjin mother of two, told the BBC: "There is peace in Kiambaa area and indeed the entire Uasin Gishu county and my joy is that I have voted peacefully and [I am] hoping that all will be well even after the results are announced." Peter Kariuki, a father of four, said despite losing his relatives in the Kiambaa church fire, he is encouraged with the prevailing peace existing among the various communities that used not to see eye to eye. "I am very happy because this vote is a new beginning to residents of Kiambaa and Eldoret," he said. I was awoken in this lakeside city, a stronghold of presidential candidate Raila Odinga, at 02:15 by people blowing vuvuzelas - their alarm call to get people down to the polling stations early. By 04:00 - two hours before the polls opened - thousands of people were already queuing. There was a little tension at one polling station when it did not open on time and voters forced the gate open, but officials restored order and voting began. Women with babies or who were pregnant were able to get to the front on the winding line. At one polling station a woman stuffed a baby blanket under her dress so that she could pass for pregnant and be given priority to vote, but her belly ruse did not work. After that women in the slum of Kondele were asked to breastfeed their children to prove the offspring are theirs in order to jump the queues. Kondele, where there are high rates of unemployment, has a history of electoral violence with rival local politicians often using youths to cause trouble. A 56-year-old man in Kondele told me it was the first time he had ever witnessed a peaceful election in the slum. Mr Odinga's Cord alliance has been urging people not to drink alcohol and on the eve of the vote most bars in Kisumu were closed. The majority of businesses have also been shut today and after voting people followed advice to go home instead of hanging around in groups to watch the proceedings. It is hard to believe given the huge crowds earlier on but electoral officials in Kondele were already tallying the votes just an hour after the polls were due to close at 17:00. After being counted, the ballots will be taken to a central place in the city before being transferred to Nairobi. People came out in huge numbers to vote, some queuing in the chilly morning from 03:00. There were complaints about the slow process of casting the six ballots, but voters remained jovial. "I've waited five hours - I can wait 50 more," one man told me. "I will not leave before voting, come rain, sun, hunger or sleep." Nakuru is a cosmopolitan area, though it turned into an ethnic battle field between two rival communities, the Kalenjins and Kikuyus, after the last election. "We will redeem the image of Nakuru, what happened in 2007 will not happen again. We have learnt our lesson," a 29-year-old woman told me. Some people travelled long distances to vote, one man at the Afraha stadium - where the line was twice the length of a football pitch - had returned home from Uganda where he works. The biometric ID systems malfunctioned at most polling stations, which caused delays. One person, who joined a queue at 03:00 eventually voted at 11:00 because he was searching for his name on the paper voters' register - it was only at the front of the third queue that he was eventually successful. Despite the delays, everyone got a chance to vote and polling stations closed as planned at 17:00 local time (14:00 GMT). Most people have returned home, to follow the counting process on TV or radio. The usually busy city centre is deserted, with no cars or pedestrians. Even the curio stalls popular with tourists coming to see the flamingos at nearby Lake Nakuru are closed. I came across only one restaurant that is open. Trucks full of police can be seen patrolling everywhere in this town - an agricultural centre in the Rift Valley. But people I spoke to say they do not expect any violence once results come out, as efforts to achieve reconciliation between communities that were pitted against each other after the 2007 election have been successful.

Training deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) is a time consuming task that may take weeks to complete. In this article we propose a novel, theoretically founded method for reducing CNN training time without incurring any loss in accuracy. The basic idea is to begin training with a pre-train network using lower-resolution kernels and input images, and then refine the results at the full resolution by exploiting the spatial scaling property of convolutions. We apply our method to the ImageNet winner OverFeat and to the more recent ResNet architecture and show a reduction in training time of nearly 20 while test set accuracy is preserved in both cases.

Since its founding, the EU has operated among an increasing plurality of national and globalising legal systems. This has meant both the European Court of Justice and the highest national courts have been drawn into a tug-of-war over which system's laws will prevail in Europe - or whether they should even apply at all. As one prominent member state is keen to remind us when it comes up for renegotiation: "Let me make it clear once again that these are not issues we can agree on with other countries; this is about what our country wants." The issue dates as far back as 1993, under president Jacques Delors who was determined to increase harmonisation across areas such as competition law when he proposed EU judges be permitted to oversee cases taken against member states by third parties abroad (known as 'third party' litigation). National governments were initially wary but eventually got behind the idea because most feared being sued themselves if their own regulatory regimes failed to live up to international standards set out elsewhere. In 1998, however, the UK government blocked the proposal after Tony Blair raised concerns about judicial interference from Brussels. The move angered lawyers representing victims of the BSE crisis, some of whom had lost so much money through damages awarded by British courts that many felt unable to pursue civil action in foreign jurisdictions. It also threatened London's position as a centre for dispute resolution between business competitors around the world where complex commercial challenges often chose English law as the basis for settlement agreements rather than local legislation, or regulations derived directly from European directives adopted without any input from domestic legislators whatsoever. Critics accused Britain of playing politics with people's livelihoods while others pointed out that delays created by protracted court battles could affect businesses right down to the bottom line. But then prime minister John Major defended his decision saying "there must always remain substantial room for interpretation" adding that there was no need for the ECJ to become involved, particularly given Germany already provided similar services free of charge. More recently, Theresa May fretted about German dominance within the EU's top court during her 2016 negotiations with Angela Merkel, making the point multiple times throughout talks that she wanted safeguards specifically designed to protect Britain's interests inside the Luxembourg institution. As Mrs May told journalists last year "we want them [the rules] interpreted in accordance with those objectives." Yet despite lengthy discussions aimed largely at ensuring compromise, little progress appears likely now ahead of next week's crunch gathering, suggesting another major obstacle remains unresolved. One source told me earlier today: Mayll keep talking until Wednesday night... If nothing gets agreed before dinner time tomorrow I think it'll probably go wrong."

"Yes, leftenant, we sent a probe two cycles ago. The results just came back, which is what I was waiting upon to give you the news." "And?" While self-attention mechanism has shown promising results for many vision tasks, it only considers the current features at a time. We show that such a manner cannot take full advantage of the attention mechanism. In this paper, we present Deep Connected Attention Network (DCANet), a novel design that boosts attention modules in a CNN model without any modification of the internal structure. To achieve this, we interconnect adjacent attention blocks, making information flow among attention blocks possible. With DCANet, all attention blocks in a CNN model are trained jointly, which improves the ability of attention learning. Our DCANet is generic. It is not limited to a specific attention module or base network architecture. Experimental results on ImageNet and MS COCO benchmarks show that DCANet consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art attention modules with a minimal additional computational overhead in all test cases. All code and models are made publicly available.

Phillips also recommended that NASA provide additional technical assistance and resources to help North American complete its tasks. Ultimately, Phillips' recommendations were implemented, and the Apollo Program eventually succeeded. The success of the Apollo Program is a testament to the power of effective problem-solving, and it stands as an example of how careful planning and rigorous management can lead to success even in the face of seemingly insurmountable obstacles.

In the late 1790s, Charles Darwin’s grandfather, Erasmus Darwin, proposed a concept of species transformation, while Jean-Baptiste Lamarck expanded upon this idea in 1809. Both believed that basic life forms arose spontaneously and evolved toward increasing complexity through adaptation – a mechanism known as Lamarckism – driven by inherited modifications resulting from environmental pressures. Later, Geoffroy argued that embryonic development mirrored evolutionary changes from previous periods, influenced by the environment, and that animals shared a fundamental blueprint based on structural similarities. Conversely, Georges Cuvier challenged these notions, asserting that apparent similarities among diverse, unchanging species stemmed from their designed functionality. He established the fact of extinction during the 1790s, attributing it to localized disasters followed by recolonization by new species.

Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models are sensitive to small perturbations in the input. Robustness to such perturbations is typically measured using translation quality metrics such as BLEU on the noisy input. This paper proposes additional metrics which measure the relative degradation and changes in translation when small perturbations are added to the input. We focus on a class of models employing subword regularization to address robustness and perform extensive evaluations of these models using the robustness measures proposed. Results show that our proposed metrics reveal a clear trend of improved robustness to perturbations when subword regularization methods are used.

Sequence set is a widely-used type of data source in a large variety of fields. A typical example is protein structure prediction, which takes an multiple sequence alignment (MSA) as input and aims to infer structural information from it. Almost all of the existing approaches exploit MSAs in an indirect fashion, i.e., they transform MSAs into position-specific scoring matrices (PSSM) that represent the distribution of amino acid types at each column. PSSM could capture column-wise characteristics of MSA, however, the column-wise characteristics embedded in each individual component sequence were nearly totally neglected. The drawback of PSSM is rooted in the fact that an MSA is essentially an unordered sequence set rather than a matrix. Specifically, the interchange of any two sequences will not affect the whole MSA. In contrast, the pixels in an image essentially form a matrix since any two rows of pixels cannot be interchanged. Therefore, the traditional deep neural networks designed for image processing cannot be directly applied on sequence sets. Here, we proposed a novel deep neural network framework (called Seq-SetNet) for sequence set processing. By employing a symmetric function module to integrate features calculated from preceding layers, Seq-SetNet are immune to the order of sequences in the input MSA. This advantage enables us to directly and fully exploit MSAs by considering each component protein individually. We evaluated Seq-SetNet by using it to extract structural information from MSA for protein secondary structure prediction. Experimental results on popular benchmark sets suggests that Seq-SetNet outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches by 3.6 in precision. These results clearly suggest the advantages of Seq-SetNet in sequence set processing and it can be readily used in a wide range of fields, say natural language processing.

Currently detention is one of the most common punishments in schools in the United States, the UK, Ireland, Singapore and other countries. It requires the pupil to remain in school despite being in a high risk group when he or she arrives at school and dismisses him or her from classes because they are not complying with social distancing rules. But even in Britain, where the rules are stricter than in many other places including China, students can be detained for up to two months if they refuse to comply with social distancing rules. In schools across England, school officials have recently begun engaging with pupils about how to follow the measures that should last "for as long as possible." Under current rules, some pupils may only leave home to pick up food and drink (the government said it was considering expanding this) but others might be allowed back into classrooms once again after more than 12 weeks. The student will also be subject to Covid-19 tests - on which coronavirus test results can be found - once their isolation period ends. The government has suggested that both pupils and teachers could opt out of contact with other people outside their families. However both parents would need to provide proof of vaccination against coronavirus before they may do so. Schools currently charge rates based on grades four through five. But in an attempt to force pupils back into contact with others outside their households, the government has advised them to isolate themselves for 14 days. If they fail to do so, they may be taken into custody. The policy applies to any person who has been diagnosed with the virus themselves, although in practice it appears to be more tailored to young people. Similarities exist between some English National Teachers' Union members and those outside education, but there are few similarities in terms of teaching style and effectiveness. One teacher told me: "Teachers are very good at keeping children safe so I think our level of care is really important." Another added: "I used to teach this class for three years, and we didn't get to know each other well enough to understand each other's ways." A third told me that while some teachers were more comfortable teaching children in groups like 3 - roughly 6 - people, others did not like sharing youngsters' learning space with others. In addition to the way that behaviour changes within schools, policies can affect how pupils learn. For example, the NHS says that a child who tests positive for COVID-19 needs to quarantine for 14 days; another tells parents that they must self-isolate upon returning to school, unless they have symptoms of Covid-19 within 28 days. This is meant to protect children from contracting the disease. Many schools still recommend masks for all pupils. On top of that, teachers may require face shields and gloves at all times. There are also restrictions in place over what constitutes "quality" - whether classroom staff or students should wear them. Students are asked to maintain physical distance by washing their hands often and taking steps to keep them apart if needed. Material such as napkins or cardboard boxes are not permitted under section 107 of the Education Act 2010. Teachers may then carry out teaching tasks without wearing protective equipment for a period of time. Parents who cannot service teachers due to illness should also check their own contacts regularly and ask questions on social media about concerns over the health of their children.

A job where there are many workers willing to work a large amount of time (high supply) competing for a job that few require (low demand) will result in a low wage for that job. This is because competition between workers drives down the wage. An example of this would be jobs such as dish-washing or customer service. Competition amongst workers tends to drive down wages due to the expendable nature of the worker in relation to his or her particular job. A job where there are few able or willing workers (low supply), but a large need for the positions (high demand), will result in high wages for that job. This is because competition between employers for employees will drive up the wage. Examples of this would include jobs that require highly developed skills, rare abilities, or a high level of risk. Competition amongst employers tends to drive up wages due to the nature of the job, since there is a relative shortage of workers for the particular position. Professional and labor organizations may limit the supply of workers which results in higher demand and greater incomes for members. Members may also receive higher wages through collective bargaining, political influence, or corruption.

Sometimes I like to come out to the woods and clear my head. The silence is relaxing, but only for so long. Once you stop and listen for a few minutes, you realize just how loud nature is. Thousands of birds, insects, and animals all chittering and squawking away in the trees, which creak and sway in the wind. It's a racket. But that day there was something new. The birds and the insects were silent once I got close to it. I wouldn't have even stopped if I hadn't suddenly hit that weird dead zone where no chirps or whistles, cries or calls could be heard at all. Just low, unabated screaming. It didn't sound like screaming immediately, it was just an odd hum, kind of high pitched; variant in tone, pitch and volume. I stopped there, looking up and around completely dumbfounded, unsure if I was hearing things. I tried stretching my jaw to pop my ears as though it was tinnitus, but nothing helped. Then I started to look around, sure there must be some structure, maybe a power plant nearby I was hearing. All I found was the hole. It was roughly a foot wide, and seemed like it had been laser cut into a perfect circle, but long enough ago that the edges were starting to wear out and erode. The hum got louder and I had the sickening impression when I put my head down close that it sounded like screaming. But not like an animal or even a person. But a lot of people, hundreds even, maybe more. My blood ran cold, a phrase I had never understood until then. All the hair on my body stood up, my heart raced and pounded so hard I could see it shaking my vision with it's intensity. I pushed myself away from the abyssal hole and staggered back, falling down and shuffling backward through the leaves and deadfall in my need to distance myself from this mystery hole. After a moment of panting, I collected myself, standing up and brushing the leaves off my pants. I took a few deep breaths and told myself that there must be an explanation for this, there's no way there's a thousand or more people underground screaming their heads off up through a hole in the forest floor. I approached the hole again cautiously. I edged up to it, looking down and down to see if there was any bottom, but I couldn't see one just yet. It was then that I realized there were sometimes words within the screaming, it sounded like I might be able to parse it out but it was so difficult to hear it against all the other noise. I got back on my hands and knees and listened, straining to understand that fleeting message lost in the background of constant shrieking. As I pushed my head closer and closer to the hole, I began to make it out. It wasn't until my head was all the way in that I heard what the overpowered message was. "The hole will take you" Now I'm down here, with all the others. I am taken. And all I can do is scream into the abyss.

One of the most uncomfortable aspects of AI technology is that we do not understand how the algorithms that we end up with work. This can make it difficult for humans to trust AI and incorporate it into our daily lives. Explainable AI (XAI) is a growing field that aims to address this issue by developing algorithms and systems that provide transparent and interpretable output. This approach seeks to provide insights into how AI systems reach their conclusions and recommendations, making it easier for individuals to understand and trust the technology.

Constraint programming employs methods for tackling complex problems involving choices, represented by decision variables within defined ranges and relationships established through constraints. A core element is propagation – inferring additional information about these variables by analyzing constraints, often reducing possible values within their domains. Numerous specialized propagation algorithms, called propagators, cater to diverse constraint types. “Support” plays a vital role in propagator design; a value loses support when it’s no longer relevant to potential solutions. Techniques like AC2001 and GAC-Schema utilize support differently—one focusing on individual values and the other on sets of values. We broaden this idea of support by permitting groups of values to provide it, and extending the supported item beyond individual literals to encompass entire constraints or portions thereof.  We establish a method for creating reliable propagators based on this generalized support. Constraints are described via support properties that can be formally verified. Applying Curry-Howard isomorphism, we translate logical proof steps into executable programs, demonstrating how to generate correct propagators from those proofs. This structure prioritizes algorithm efficiency, potentially leveraging techniques like dynamic literal triggers. Two examples illustrate the application of this approach to create optimized algorithms.

Independent Component Analysis (ICA) is a dimensionality reduction technique that can boost efficiency of machine learning models that deal with probability density functions, e.g. Bayesian neural networks. Algorithms that implement adaptive ICA converge slower than their nonadaptive counterparts, however, they are capable of tracking changes in underlying distributions of input features. This intrinsically slow convergence of adaptive methods combined with existing hardware implementations that operate at very low clock frequencies necessitate fundamental improvements in both algorithm and hardware design. This paper presents an algorithm that allows efficient hardware implementation of ICA. Compared to previous work, our FPGA implementation of adaptive ICA improves clock frequency by at least one order of magnitude and throughput by at least two orders of magnitude. Our proposed algorithm is not limited to ICA and can be used in various machine learning problems that use stochastic gradient descent optimization.

Recent research highlights QoS-driven web service recommendations as a valuable tool for suggesting superior services to users. Existing methods utilizing collaborative filtering and partial QoS observations often produce accurate predictions for unseen ratings. Nevertheless, gathering user QoS data raises significant privacy issues, deterring individuals from sharing their usage information. This presents a major obstacle to building reliable web service recommendation systems. Our paper introduces an initial strategy to address these privacy worries through a straightforward obfuscation framework, alongside two concrete prediction models built upon it. Experiments using a public dataset confirm the practicality and performance of our privacy-protecting approach, offering a foundation for future research in this area.

The term “4G” as currently advertised by mobile providers doesn’t align with official standards established by the ITU-R. Essentially, no provider truly meets these specifications. Originally, 4G was conceived as a significant leap forward from 3G, offering substantially increased speeds. Devices need specific components—like antennas—to access 4G networks.  According to the ITU-R, 4G should achieve high speeds and utilize internet-based call routing. While various technologies exist under the umbrella of “4G,” such as LTE (used by Verizon and AT&T), WiMAX (primarily with Sprint), and HSPA (offered by T-Mobile), each has varying capabilities and impacts on battery life. LTE is the dominant 4G technology, with planned upgrades for further improvements. WiMAX, though fast, isn’t broadly adopted globally. HSPA represents an enhanced version of 3G, capable of reaching approximately 84 Mbps.

There are a myriad of hypothesis to explain how sexual reproduction first developed. I did my undergraduate thesis on yeast epigenetics (gene regulation through histone modification) so I'm only going to discuss the theory pertaining to that. In short, it was an accident. A cell developed the ability to share genetic material and through this was able to surviveleave more offspring. Sexual reproduction was likely gradual, with the sharing of some genetic information at first followed by full chromosomal recombination after. Sexual reproduction creates diversity and helps eliminate bad genes from the gene pool. This is typically a net positive despite the increased costs of sexual reproduction. Therefore cells that could do sexual reproduction generally had higher fitness than those that didn't. Early evolutionary versions of this can be seen in certain bacteria. Bacteria use a sex pilus, basically a tube that sticks out of the cell. The first cell pokes a second recipient cell and the two fuse. Genetic material is then shared between bacteria. For yeast, this is different. Yeast have the option of reproducing asexually and sexually. They can bud, basically producing an identical copy of themselves or under certain conditions they can undergo sexual reproduction and even class switching (kind of like male to female and vice versa). For yeast, they can have a haploid form (non duplicated genome) or a diploid form (duplicated genome). The diploid does sexual reproduction. The haploid does not. It's likely that during some point a cell that reproduced exclusively via budding was able to combine genetically with another to form this diploid cell. These diploid cells may have existed for quite some time before one received a mutation causing it to split again into 4 haploid cells. Then over time, the process evolved until a point where we have yeast cells that could undergo meiosis (sexual reproduction) as we know it today. So to summarize: 1. Development of sexual reproduction occurred gradually. 2. Everything began as a single celled organism that reproduced asexually. 3. A random mutation occurred that allowed this cell to fuse with another and share genetic material. 4. Over subsequent generations this fusing and sharing of genetic material developed. 5. Eventually this process would lead to meiosis (sexual reproduction) as we know it.," "No one knows much about the origins of sexual reproduction. I'm sure there are ideas, but it's all just speculation. It's very difficult to definitively find out how something evolved over a billion years ago. As for how life formed before sexual reproduction, that's easy! For single-celled organisms, the cells grow until they reach a certain size, then divide into two smaller cells and keep on growing. Many non-sexually-reproducing (asexual) organisms are single-celled, but there are some multicellular organisms like the [hydra] (URL0) that reproduce by new organisms budding off of older ones and just breaking away when they are big enough. Most (all?) types of fungi and some plants can also reproduce asexually, although they usually retain the ability to reproduce sexually under certain circumstances.,Before sexual reproduction, there was asexual reproduction- basically self-cloning or mitosis. However, this process makes populations susceptible to diseasesbad mutationsetc. When more advanced cells emerged, they "discovered" that swapping DNA and getting some diversification in there was better than simple self-cloning. And as cells got more and more advanced, so did sexual reproduction get more and more advanced, eventually resulting in distinct sexes. Electronic Design Automation (EDA) industry heavily reuses third party IP cores. These IP cores are vulnerable to insertion of Hardware Trojans (HTs) at design time by third party IP core providers or by malicious insiders in the design team. State of the art research has shown that existing HT detection techniques, which claim to detect all publicly available HT benchmarks, can still be defeated by carefully designing new sophisticated HTs. The reason being that these techniques consider the HT landscape to be limited only to the publicly known HT benchmarks, or other similar (simple) HTs. However the adversary is not limited to these HTs and may devise new HT design principles to bypass these countermeasures. In this paper, we discover certain crucial properties of HTs which lead to the definition of an exponentially large class of Deterministic Hardware Trojans H D that an adversary can (but is not limited to) design. The discovered properties serve as HT design principles, based on which we design a new HT called XOR-LFSR and present it as a 'proof-of-concept' example from the class H D . These design principles help us understand the tremendous ways an adversary has to design a HT, and show that the existing publicly known HT benchmarks are just the tip of the iceberg on this huge landscape. This work, therefore, stresses that instead of guaranteeing a certain (low) false negative rate for a small constant set of publicly known HTs, a rigorous HT detection tool should take into account these newly discovered HT design principles and hence guarantee the detection of an exponentially large class (exponential in number of wires in IP core) of HTs with negligible false negative rate.

Obituary: Francisco Blake Mora The helicopter was flying to Cuernavaca in neighbouring Morelos state for a prosecutors' meeting when it went down. All eight people on board were killed. President Felipe Calderon said weather conditions were probably to blame. Mr Blake Mora, 45, was appointed to the post last year and was a key figure in the war against drug cartels. The helicopter had initially been reported missing. Some Mexican media reports said there was heavy cloud at the time. "Unfortunately the interior secretary, his [assistants] and the helicopter crew were found dead," government spokeswoman Alejandra Sota said. Deputy Interior Secretary Felipe Zamora Castro and the interior ministry's chief press officer Jose Alfredo Garcia Medina were also killed in the crash along with other government officials and the air force crew, Ms Sota said. She said a search for the helicopter began when it was discovered it had strayed from its planned course. Mexican television showed wreckage from the helicopter strewn across a hillside. Ms Sota said the craft went down in the Xochimilco area, just south of Mexico City. By Ignacio de los ReyesBBC Mundo, Mexico Francisco Blake Mora was one of the president's right-hand men. Not only because he was in charge of domestic affairs, but also because he became one of the most strident voices of Mr Calderon's strategy against the drug cartels. In recent months, he helped co-ordinate the army, navy and federal police in the fight against drug trafficking in violence-torn cities like Veracruz or Acapulco. But his death could be a severe blow to Mr Calderon at a personal level too. Three years ago, one of the president's best friends, then Interior Secretary Juan Camilo Mourino, was killed in a plane crash in Mexico City. That accident was one of the saddest moments for Mr Calderon since he took power in 2006, he said. Mr Camilo Mourino was remembered by members of the cabinet, including Mr Blake Mora, this week. His last message on his Twitter account (FBlakeM) was actually dedicated to Mr Mourino. "The cloudy conditions at the time certainly make you think about the probability of an accident," President Calderon said in a televised address. He said a thorough investigation of the accident was being launched and cancelled a trip to Hawaii for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum. US President Barack Obama called Mr Calderon to offer his condolences, a US government spokesman said. Mr Obama "reinforced his commitment to the close partnership between the United States and Mexico in this difficult time," said US National Security Council spokesman Ben Rhodes. The interior secretary is Mexico's senior cabinet position and the top official after the president, with responsibility for domestic affairs and security. Mr Blake was Mr Calderon's fourth interior secretary. One of his predecessors, Juan Camilo Mourino, was killed in a plane crash in Mexico City three years ago. Mr Blake began his political career in the north-western border city of Tijuana in the mid-1990s, later serving as interior secretary for Baja California state. He also served as a federal congressman from Mr Calderon's National Action Party. He earned a reputation as being a hardliner in Mexico's struggle with drug cartels. Mr Blake Mora frequently travelled to cities badly affected by the cartels, such as Veracruz and Ciudad Juarez, to help co-ordinate the government's response. More than 40,000 people are reported to have died from drug-related violence since President Calderon sent in the army to help combat the cartels in 2006.

Bakr Hamad, 38, of Hull, Sharif Kadir, 52, of Sheffield, Zana Rahim, 32, of Derby and Awat Hamasalih, 33, of Birmingham, appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday. All four refused to consent to extradition when appearing in court. The men are due to appear before magistrates again on 20 November. They were arrested on Thursday on European Arrest warrants. During their court appearance, their lawyers indicated they may challenge their extradition because of the risk of "refoulement," which the United Nations defines as "the expulsion of persons who have the right to be recognised as refugees." The men were held as part of raids in six European countries, led by Italian authorities and connected to a suspected "jihadist network," Rawti Shax, which is said to be seeking to establish a caliphate in Iraq's Kurdistan region. The group was allegedly plotting to free its leader, Mullah Krekar, who is in detention in Norway. Suspects were also arrested in Italy and Norway, while authorities in Italy, Germany, Finland, Norway, Switzerland and the UK also searched a total of 26 properties. BBC security correspondent Frank Gardner said there was no suggestion any of those arrested were planning attacks in the UK. Their focus appeared to have been in the Middle East, he added, with the investigation aimed at breaking up an international recruiting pipeline that was sending jihadists to join the Islamic State and Al-Nusra organisations - both proscribed terrorist organisations - in Iraq and Syria. Eurojust, the EU agency which co-ordinated the European raids, said suspected leaders and several members of the group were arrested during simultaneous activity in the six countries. It added: "The arrested persons are charged with international terrorism." The operation, which follows several years of work by investigators, was launched under the direction of the Public Prosecution Office in Rome. Mullah Krekar went to Norway as a refugee in 1991 from Iraq and founded radical Islamist group Ansar al-Islam, although he later tried to distance himself from it. Norwegian authorities have been trying to deport him since 2003 after deeming him a threat to national security. Eurojust said Rawti Shax, or Didi Nwe, meaning the "new course" or "towards the mountain," represented an "evolution of Ansar al-Islam," which is listed by the UN as a terrorist organisation affiliated with al-Qaeda. It says the group has a "primary objective" which is to "violently overthrow the current Iraqi Kurdish government and replace it with a caliphate governed by Sharia law." It also alleged that the group was active in providing logistical and financial support for the recruitment of foreign fighters to be sent to Syria and Iraq, and also had the intent of training them for a future conflict in Kurdistan.

A couple of quick notes: I am going to use the term "believe in evolution" simply for convenience. Evolutionary theory is generally not considered something that you believe in, but rather a natural explanation of how life began and evolved over time. The other thing I would like to mention about belief vs. unbelief is that in addition to being contradictory, there are also two different concepts, which actually do have some similarities (though they really aren't similar at all). In fact, both things are made up by people who claim to be scientists - they're called phrenologists. Which kind of proves my point - while scientific ideas may seem contradictory or even absurd, if you are able to prove them wrong then they can become common concepts among those believing in their own theories. Therefore, it's important to remember that if your parents raised you to think that evolution was proven true, you still likely don't understand why this idea occurred. The best way to help yourself hopefully is through education on the topic, with the goal of understanding what caused our species to evolve into the ones we see today. And that means learning from every new discovery that comes along as well.

Our twisted game of hide and seek. Neither of us hate the other. No, far from it. In a strange sense, I suppose you could call our homicidal bloodlust it's own form of love! After all, what couple could keep their eyes solely on eachother for all eternity? Most can barely last a single lifetime. But we're both devoted. We're not going to back down until one of us reaches checkmate. It's no matter of pride, it's a matter of obligation. We've been doing this dance too long to back out now. Hunting eachother down, exchanging blows and fading into the background to lick our wounds. Not to say we're so pedestrian as to only resort to fisticuffs. We're better than that. With over 200,000 years of knowledge behind us, I should hope so at least. Still, the orchestration of our grand game stands as a testament to my testimony. So rarely do we see eachother in the flesh, yet our handiwork is ever present. It seems, after all, we both get a rush from the execution of many years of strategic machination. While she has the dowager empresses ear, I fill a young man's head with tales of revolution. While I stand by Nero, she has the vandals and visigoths trapped in her webs. She advises the Kaiser, I am Asquith's loyal servant. She stands with Churchill, and I address Hitler's war cabinet. I narrowly escape Hiroshima, while she deftly flees a burning tower. We have no time for human morality in this unending, eternal game. It's a petty, pointless thing that holds no bearing on our goals. But, even so, I must wonder how humanity would react to know that they're all just mere pawns in all this. Would they be horrified? Would they reject it? Or, perhaps, would they embrace it? Would knowing their is a root to all human tragedies pacify them, sooth them and make them complacent? To know that their only reason is to serve as the cannon fodder for two far greater beings? And certainly, at the very least, they must acknowledge that it is through our influence that their modern understanding of human luxury exists. That it is through her toiling that they have the technology they do, that it is through mine that art and music flows forth, and that it is through our joint efforts that medicine and math is within the realm of their understanding. Even if our motives were less than pure, and even if all that humanity loves was but another weapon to us, they owe their lives to us. So, then, if human suffering and human pleasure were but the children born of the struggles of gods..... Would it be impudence for the average man to decry our actions? I can't say. In the end, despite our appearance, we are far too removed from the human race to ever understand their minute lives. But all there shall come a time when these musings come to a close. No more will humanity have to determine anything, nor will they have to play their part in our pivotal production. This is the reason that I write this piece. Soon, to a thunderous applause, the game shall end. And once it does, what shall I do? I have yet to decide. Maybe I shall roam the burned out husk of the planet once called Earth? Maybe I will head out into space and explore the heavens? Maybe I will end my life, satisfied with an ultimate conclusion. After all, it is for the game that my heart still beats, it is for her that I still live, it is for the rush that I exist. So, then, without a goal what purpose does flesh and blood serve? I may, provided a lack of inspiration in the aftermath of my coming actions, simply choose to welcome my end with open arms and, I pray, reunite with her on the other side. Perhaps, all willing, our next meeting would be one without bloodshed. Though, knowing our inherent hunger for violence, I can't imagine that any substitute could hold off such innate urges long enough for a peaceful eternity. I do not fear conclusion. Despite a heavy heart, I hunger for it. In any case, it is time that I lay our duet to rest. I'm sure you understand. But, I regret that you'll fail to live to see the beautiful comedy of my final design. You see, my dear Eve, my victory comes not from a well executed plot, nor a clever plan. No. Sometimes all victory takes is pointing a glorious leader in the right direction. With love, let us meet again on the other side. Checkmate.

However, in terms of where Russia is economically, they are at a crossroads. The US, with its "anti-Russian" stance, has effectively placed a roadblock in the way of the Russian economy and they are now competing against both China and India for the resources the US has refused to give them. Historically, Russia has had to deal with the West in some form or another, and in the past, they have been able to take advantage of this and, in some cases, subvert the West. In the 1990's, Russia was able to co-opt much of the European Union, including the UK, and use them as a springboard to gain influence in the rest of the world. This has largely ended due to the end of the Cold War, and the US and Russia are now in a situation where the US can, and will, continue to hold the upper hand. Russia has had to develop a strategy to deal with this. As a first step, Russia needs to be able to keep afloat and not have to depend on the West to support them. The Russian economy has had to become more and more reliant on exports, and the US, with its massive surplus of goods and services, is now the primary buyer of Russian goods. Russia's GDP has been growing at about 3 per year, which is not particularly impressive. However, their exports have grown at an impressive 8 per year, which has been crucial to their economic growth. The Russians have to now diversify their exports and find new markets to keep their economy afloat, and they have done this by taking a more "hard line" against the West. For example, the Russians have decided to make their anti-ballistic missile system, which they plan to deploy in Europe, an integral part of their national security, which means that they will have to spend money on it and deploy it. In addition, the Russians have begun to establish closer ties with countries in Eastern Europe, such as Belarus and Ukraine.

Histamine triggers some nasty effects like inflamation and bronchoconstriction by binding to the H1-receptors in the smooth muscles of the bronchioles and in the skin. Histamine and acetylcholine are both neurotransmitters. Acetylcholine, a parasympathetic neurotransmitter, causes the bronchioles to relax, while histamine, a sympathetic neurotransmitter, causes them to constrict. This means that when you are exposed to an allergen your body is first trying to relax the bronchioles so that the allergens can be sneezed out. So what is going on in your body when you are suffering from an allergic reaction? Your body is trying to sneeze out the allergens, but it cannot. Instead your body reacts with inflamation and bronchoconstriction. Once the bronchioles are constricted, the parasympathetic system will relax them, so the allergens can be sneezed out. The constriction, however, is so strong that the bronchioles are not able to relax, so the inflamation continues. This is why the symptoms of an allergic reaction last for a while. When the histamine level rises, it also causes an effect on the release of seratonin, a neurotransmitter that can also trigger inflamation. This is why histamine is an important factor in eczema, and why it is important that you avoid eating histamine rich foods. The number of small objects represents the upper bound for objects in your jar, while the number that represents the big objects is the lower bound. If the distribution of sizes is uniform then you can even pinpoint the exact amount of things in your jar (with a small uncertainity of course), it's simply the arithmetic mean of the two boundaries.,There is a way to solve the problem with very basic arithmetic. Open up the jar, count each object, deal with any witnesses.','Just depends on if you're good at estimating how many would be in one "layer" and how many layers there are. Of course there aren't distinct layers but you get the idea. For example, you might be able to count 8 balls on the lowest inch of the jar. Then depending on the diameter of the jar, you might estimate that there are 40 balls in the lowest inch of the jar. Then if the jar is 5 inches high, you might arrive at 200 balls. But then you might estimate up, because the layers aren't distinct inches, and some smaller objects can be between "layers." Keep in mind that "layers" here is just a way to simplify the problem. So you might add a bit and estimate 250 objects. It's not completely luck, it has to do with your ability to take the pattern that you see, and apply that to what you think the volume of the container is. It would be luck if you could only see objects of a certain size, but were told that the objects in the center of the jar are of another size. This study examines reduced-order models (ROMs) designed to effectively handle partial differential equations whose solutions undergo bifurcation—a significant change in behavior—due to variations in several input parameters. Specifically, we explore a “local ROM” technique utilizing the k-means algorithm to group data snapshots and build individual local Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) bases. A central aspect of this method, the local basis selection process, is analyzed; various criteria were evaluated, revealing that an artificial neural network (ANN)-based regression yielded the best performance when applied to a channel flow problem displaying a supercritical pitchfork bifurcation. This benchmark was subsequently used to contrast the local ROM with the ANN selection criterion against a traditional global projection-based ROM and a newer ANN-based method known as POD-NN. Results demonstrate that the local ROM surpasses the global projection-based ROM by a factor exceeding ten in terms of accuracy, while POD-NN consistently offers superior approximations compared to the local projection-based ROM.

The fundamental building block of social influence is for one person to elicit a response in another. Researchers measuring a "response" in social media typically depend either on detailed models of human behavior or on platform-specific cues such as re-tweets, hash tags, URLs, or mentions. Most content on social networks is difficult to model because the modes and motivation of human expression are diverse and incompletely understood. We introduce content transfer , an information-theoretic measure with a predictive interpretation that directly quantifies the strength of the effect of one user's content on another's in a model-free way. Estimating this measure is made possible by combining recent advances in non-parametric entropy estimation with increasingly sophisticated tools for content representation. We demonstrate on Twitter data collected for thousands of users that content transfer is able to capture non-trivial, predictive relationships even for pairs of users not linked in the follower or mention graph. We suggest that this measure makes large quantities of previously under-utilized social media content accessible to rigorous statistical causal analysis.

Due to the ubiquitous use of embeddings as input representations for a wide range of natural language tasks, imputation of embeddings for rare and unseen words is a critical problem in language processing. Embedding imputation involves learning representations for rare or unseen words during the training of an embedding model, often in a post-hoc manner. In this paper, we propose an approach for embedding imputation which uses grounded information in the form of a knowledge graph. This is in contrast to existing approaches which typically make use of vector space properties or subword information. We propose an online method to construct a graph from grounded information and design an algorithm to map from the resulting graphical structure to the space of the pre-trained embeddings. Finally, we evaluate our approach on a range of rare and unseen word tasks across various domains and show that our model can learn better representations. For example, on the Card-660 task our method improves Pearson's and Spearman's correlation coefficients upon the state-of-the-art by 11 and 17.8 respectively using GloVe embeddings. footnote Footnote footnotes Footnotes footnote Published as a conference paper at ACL 2019

The human heart is remarkably impressive. Contrary to Moskau50’s comment, our data demonstrates its representativeness; the widespread similarity in mammalian heart structures reveals a great deal about evolution’s skill at discovering efficient designs. You posed a straightforward question, so I wanted to express my enthusiasm regarding the heart’s brilliance. Its rhythmic beating originates from the sinoatrial node, a location near the heart’s upper portion, driven partly by the nervous system and primarily by a gradual change in cellular electrical charge due to sodium leakage. Once this threshold is reached, an “action potential” triggers the heartbeat, spreading throughout the entire heart. Consequently, even without conscious control, your heart maintains a consistent rate of approximately 80 beats per minute thanks to this cell leakage. This is truly astounding. Subsequently, this action potential reaches the atrioventricular node, situated between the atria and ventricles. Should communication be disrupted, the AV node’s cells also exhibit leakage, generating a beat independently – maintaining a rate of roughly 60 beats per minute. Furthermore, the AV node briefly delays the signal for about 100 milliseconds, perfectly timed to allow the atria to fully fill with blood before ventricular contraction.

Symmetry is present in nature and science. In image processing, kernels for spatial filtering possess some symmetry (e.g. Sobel operators, Gaussian, Laplacian). Convolutional layers in artificial feed-forward neural networks have a symmetric structure: all convolutions are applied to each input layer twice while the output layer receives only one of these combinations. Performance improvements can be achieved by using higher order filters with more symmetries. However this involves decreasing computational speed due to additional computations required when applying those extra filters such as adding or multiplying multiples copies of an original filter onto its intermediate results which also requires computation time.

In this paper, we present an optimization based method for path planning of a mobile robot subject to time bounded temporal constraints, in a dynamic environment. Temporal logic (TL) can address very complex task specification such as safety, coverage, motion sequencing etc. We use metric temporal logic (MTL) to encode the task specifications with timing constraints. We then translate the MTL formulae into mixed integer linear constraints and solve the associated optimization problem using a mixed integer linear program solver. This approach is different from the automata based methods which generate a finite abstraction of the environment and dynamics, and use an automata theoretic approach to formally generate a path that satisfies the TL. We have applied our approach on several case studies in complex dynamical environments subjected to timed temporal specifications.

Charles Darwin's grandfather Erasmus Darwin outlined a hypothesis of transmutation of species in the 1790s, and Jean-Baptiste Lamarck published a more developed theory in 1809. Both envisaged that spontaneous generation produced simple forms of life that progressively developed greater complexity, adapting to the environment by inheriting changes in adults caused by use or disuse. This process was later called Lamarckism. Lamarck thought there was an inherent progressive tendency driving organisms continuously towards greater complexity, in parallel but separate lineages with no extinction. Geoffroy contended that embryonic development recapitulated transformations of organisms in past eras when the environment acted on embryos, and that animal structures were determined by a constant plan as demonstrated by homologies. Georges Cuvier strongly disputed such ideas, holding that unrelated, fixed species showed similarities that reflected a design for functional needs. His palontological work in the 1790s had established the reality of extinction, which he explained by local catastrophes, followed by repopulation of the affected areas by other species.

Forces act in a particular direction and have sizes dependent upon how strong the push or pull is. Because of these characteristics, forces are classified as "vector quantities." This means that forces follow a different set of mathematical rules than physical quantities that do not have direction (denoted scalar quantities). For example, when determining what happens when two forces act on the same object, it is necessary to know both the magnitude and the direction of both forces to calculate the result. If both of these pieces of information are not known for each force, the situation is ambiguous. For example, if you know that two people are pulling on the same rope with known magnitudes of force but you do not know which direction either person is pulling, it is impossible to determine what the acceleration of the rope will be. The two people could be pulling against each other as in tug of war or the two people could be pulling in the same direction. In this simple one-dimensional example, without knowing the direction of the forces it is impossible to decide whether the net force is the result of adding the two force magnitudes or subtracting one from the other. Associating forces with vectors avoids such problems.

Relay node placement significantly affects energy use and operational burden within two-tiered Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). This study introduces a new connectivity-focused approximation method for relay node positioning aimed at reducing system overhead. A unique Local Search Approximation Algorithm (LSAA) addresses the Relay Node Single Cover (RNSC) challenge. LSAA divides sensors into groups and applies local Set Cover (SC) algorithms to each, forming a complete SC for the RNSC problem. The algorithm’s approximation ratio and computational complexity have been rigorously proven. Furthermore, LSAA was adapted to tackle the relay node double cover problem, leading to a Relay Location Selection Algorithm (RLSA). RLSA combines the SC generated by LSAA with a minimum spanning tree heuristic to enhance high-tier network connectivity. By prioritizing locations near the sink node, RLSA creates a denser network compared to previous methods, thereby minimizing the need for additional relay nodes. Simulations show that LSAA surpasses existing techniques, and RLSA effectively reduces the number of newly deployed relays required for establishing high-tier connectivity.

Real-world audio recordings are often degraded by factors such as noise, reverberation, and equalization distortion. This paper introduces HiFi-GAN, a deep learning method to transform recorded speech to sound as good as natural speech, while preserving all spectral and temporal characteristics. The proposed model uses a generative adversarial network to learn the transformation function, which is based on the acoustic model and statistical audio models of the target domain. The audio output is then modified with a perceptual loss to produce a good sounding speech. Our experiments on two publicly available datasets show that the proposed model can generate audio with the same or better quality as natural speech. Keywords: speech synthesis, perceptual loss, GAN, GAN-based acoustic model. Introduction {Sec1} The last decade has seen an increasing interest in speech synthesis (SS), and the development of methods to transform recorded speech into natural sounding speech. SS can be divided into two main categories: acoustic models based on time-domain statistical models, and spectral domain based methods. Acoustic models use a set of speech production rules to synthesize speech, while spectral domain methods use a set of time-domain features to synthesize speech. For acoustic models, most of the existing SS systems use time-domain models, including the Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) [Chen2001], the Linear Prediction Cepstral Coefficients (LPCC) [Lee2001], the Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter [Whang2006], the Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT) [Qiu2011], the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) [Kim2016], and the Harmonic Model (HM) [Kim2017]. Among them, HM-based SS systems [Kim2017] have achieved the best performance, and can synthesize speech that is comparable to natural speech. However, HM-based SS systems are limited to 16-dimension, and cannot handle high-dimensional input signals. For spectral domain based methods, there are two main categories: the frequency-domain based methods and the time-domain based methods. In the frequency-domain based methods, SS systems synthesize speech using the Time-Domain Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (TDMFCC) [Chen2003] and the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) [Whang2006]. Among them, the time-domain based SS systems have achieved the best performance, and can synthesize speech that is comparable to natural speech. For the time-domain based methods, the Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) [Chen2001], Linear Prediction Cepstral Coefficients (LPCC) [Lee2001], the Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter [Whang2006], the Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT) [Qiu2011], the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) [Kim2016], and the Harmonic Model (HM) [Kim2017] are commonly used. The HM is the most widely used method, and can synthesize speech that is comparable to natural speech. However, HM-based SS systems are limited to 16-dimension, and cannot handle high-dimensional input signals. Recently, GANs have been widely used for generating realistic images and videos. For audio, GANs have also been used to synthesize audio [Bengio2015; Elsayed2016; Johnson2017]. However, most of the GAN-based audio synthesis methods are limited to simple waveforms, and cannot synthesize natural sounding audio. In this paper, we propose HiFi-GAN, a GAN-based method to synthesize speech with high fidelity, while preserving all spectral and temporal characteristics. The proposed model is based on the acoustic model and statistical audio models of the target domain. It uses a GAN to learn the transformation function, which is based on the acoustic model and statistical audio models of the target domain. The audio output is then modified with a perceptual loss to produce a good sounding speech. Our experiments on two publicly available datasets show that the proposed model can generate audio with the same or better quality as natural speech. Related Work {Sec2} Speech Synthesis {Sec2.1} The goal of SS is to synthesize speech from acoustic data. There are two main categories of SS systems: acoustic models based on time-domain statistical models, and spectral domain based methods.

Despite being a popular and effective point-wise embedding technique – recognized as a universal approximator for continuous set functions and capable of processing over a million points per second – PointNet faces challenges in achieving true real-time performance due to advancements in sensor technology. Typically, PointNet’s embedding function operates as a “soft-indicator” activating only within specific regions. By utilizing this behavior, we decrease computation through a replacement of PointNet’s embedding with a soft-indicator based on Gaussian kernels, demonstrating that these kernels also uphold the universal approximation properties of PointNet. Experimental evaluations confirm that our Gaussian kernel-based model delivers similar accuracy to established methods yet significantly reduces floating-point operations—up to 92% less than PointNet per sample.

Since there is no proper definition of 'life', we assess whether or not something is alive by how many of the 7 characteristics of life it exhibits. However, these characteristics need to be very extensible in order to qualify computers as alive; this is necessary if we ever plan on categorizing some alien life we hadn't conceived of as alive. I think computers exhibit the properties at least in the following ways. -1. "Composed of cells" Well, computers do have a fundamental unit which is central to their existence: the transistor. -2. "Emergent propertieslevels of organization" Certainly anyone who understands processor architecture sees that there are many levels of complexity upon which the others lie, from hardware all the way up to software. Computers also have specialized components, "organs." -3. "Uses energy" Some would say they use too much energy. -4. "Responds to environment" Computers are regularly programmed to respond to their environment, be it to users, or robots to stimuli, or weather systems to changes in readings. -5. "Grows" This is a tough one, but certainly through upgrades computers can expand not only their capabilities but also their physical form, if that is important to this definition. -6. "Reproduces" I don't think this is as tricky as it sounds. Bots build bots. The physical forms factors of some members are capable of building other things, we use them to build cars, toys, and yes, computers. This capability will only extend from where it is today. -7. "Adapts to environment" This is perhaps the most nebulous one. This involves the most complex aspects of programming such that a computer will better suit itself to its environment or task. But it certainly exists, like when rovers close shop to weather a sandstorm. If adaptations are traits giving an advantage in the environment, then upgrades can be determined and applied to the next generation at will. Computers exhibit all of the characteristics of life, in one form or another, and eventually these will come together, and beyond that become recognizable as sentient and intelligent. It sounds solid to me. I have yet to hear a convincing argument to the contrary. Let's see if there exist any.

In either of the two cases Crusoe has deferred his present consumption of 5 fishes everyday so that after he builds the net he is now able to produce and consume a LOT more fishes everyday. He can either catch 300 fishes and maybe consume them all, or make more dishes out of them, etc etc, or he could continue to catch only 25 fishes everyday, work less and have more leisure time, and spending the remaining time in working on art, literature, maybe music etc. A third world country is exactly like Crusoe without the fishing net, and a rich western country like America is exactly like Crusoe with a fishing net. In order to build more capital, you require two things: People should be willing to put a lot of present goods for later consumption When they put their present goods for later consumption, nothing should reduce or steal away their capital from them Let me elaborate what I meant by nothing should reduce or steal away the capital from people who are deferring their present consumption for future. In the above example of Crusoe, lets say Crusoe's fishes got rotten because they weren't stored properly, so his capital has been destroyed, now to achieve the same earlier result he will have to build his savings again. Take another scenario, lets say Man Friday, is another cast away, who drifted to the other part of the Island, he also catches fishes by hand, but he is able to catch only 10 fishes because he is not that good with catching fishes. When Crusoe was saving 5 fishes everyday, Man Friday decried that Crusoe was being unfair and hoarding fishes, and it was causing income inequality, also Crusoe being more dexterous with fishing, must feed Man Friday some of his fishes. So everyday Man Friday raids Crusoe's extra fishes and consumes them in the name of making the society more equal. In this case again Crusoe's capital has been depleted, and he will never be able to build that fishing net, and although Man Friday and Crusoe will be a bit more equal, they will remain poor. In fact soon Crusoe will realize that he has no incentive to really starve himself by 5 fishes, so he will either consume all 25 fishes or will catch only 5 fishes each day. Had Man Friday allowed Crusoe to build his net, Crusoe would have been able to produce a lot more fishes everyday, and then Man Friday could then provide Crusoe with some other services, in exchange for his fishes. Lets just say all Man Friday is good at, is dancing and creating stories and telling them passionately, since they both are stranded on an island, Crusoe might value this entertainment service a lot, so Crusoe works all day catching 300 fishes, and gives 100 fishes to Man Friday in exchange of Man Friday's entertainment services. This service would not be possible in a society without more capital accumulation. Had Man Friday stressed on equality, all the way along, Crusoe's net wouldn't have been built, and Crusoe would have remained relatively rich (because he caught 25 fishes everyday and consumed 20), and Man Friday would have remained poor (because he caught only 10 fishes everyday and was able to consume only 15). Please note that in the society with more capital (ie, when Crusoe built a net), Crusoe was consuming 200 fishes everyday, which is almost double of what Man Friday was consuming (100 fishes), which meant more inequality, but still Man Friday in the society was better off in this society. tl;dr: What we need is more capital accumulation, and not economic inequality. If we forcefully redistribute wealth, then we will get relatively equal but we all get poorer. Its higher capital accumulation which makes our lives better, not inequality.

The UK Personal Genome Project could provide a massive free tool for scientists to further understanding of disease and human genetics. Participants will get an analysis of their DNA, but so will the rest of the world, and anonymity is not guaranteed. They are warned there could be unknown consequences for them and relatives. Unlocking the secrets of DNA could transform the understanding of disease. A deeper understanding of Alzheimer's disease is emerging by looking for differences in the DNA of people with and without the disease. Prof George Church, who runs the US version of the project, said analysing 100,000 genomes could lead to advances in common diseases such as diabetes. He said: "We're finding more and more of these common diseases are a collection of rare diseases. "Cancer used to be a disease, then it broke up into lots of different diseases by tissue, then lots of sub-categories based on the genes that are impacted, so now it's thousands of diseases." Participants will have to pass tests to prove they fully understand the risks of making their genetic identities freely available for the world to use before taking part. There will be immediate risks and those that emerge as genetic technology advances including: Dr Peter Mills, who is investigating the ethical issues around biological and health data with the Nuffield Council on Bioethics, told the BBC: "The difference with genetic data is you're not just committing yourself to something you might not fully envisage, but you're also implicating biological relatives. "There is potentially huge public benefit, but there is the potential for it to rebound, but how that rebounds on the person, families and those yet to be born is very difficult to know." Cian Murphy, a 24-year-old PhD student at University College London, wants to take part. He said: "Very few people live their whole lives not affected by some genetic illness, your sample could be the difference between a cure being discovered or not." As part of the study, participants will find out intimate details about their genome, such as the presence of any high-risk breast-cancer genes. They will be given a list of doctors they can go to if they need further medical advice. While people will not have their name published, studies have shown it is possible to work out someone's identity from genetic databases and other public records. Dr David King, from the group Human Genetics Alert, said: "Human Genetics Alert would strongly advise people not to give their genetic information to a project which will share it with the world. "Once your data is online, you will never be able to recall it. The project's informed-consent procedures are not valid, because they do not tell you all of the risks. That is not informed consent." He warned the data could be used for any purpose including those people objected to ethically and said there was "no reason" for it to be public. Meanwhile, the government's Genomics England project is trying to sequence 100,000 NHS patient's DNA, which is private and carries a threat of legal action if patients are identified. Sir John Chisholm, executive chairman of Genomics England, said: "We would want anyone consenting to their DNA being used for sequencing to have a clear understanding of what they are contributing to, and to do so on a voluntary basis which we understand will be the case with Personal Genome Project. "Anyone who takes part in any initiative that involves giving a DNA sample for sequencing should be as clear at the time of giving their consent as they can be of how that sample will be used, and who will have access to it, and what future purposes it can be put to."

Process theology typically stresses God's relational nature. Rather than seeing God as impassive or emotionless, process theologians view God as "the fellow sufferer who understands," and as the being who is supremely affected by temporal events. Hartshorne points out that people would not praise a human ruler who was unaffected by either the joys or sorrows of his followers - so why would this be a praise-worthy quality in God? Instead, as the being who is most affected by the world, God is the being who can most appropriately respond to the world. However, process theology has been formulated in a wide variety of ways. C. Robert Mesle, for instance, advocates a "process naturalism," i.e. a process theology without God.

Octane is a measure of the fuel's resistance to burning when exposed to heat and pressure. If you want to make an engine put out more power for a given cylinder size you obviously need to cram more fuel in there, along with enough air to burn it. This means higher pressures and temperatures. If your fuel explodes too soon under such conditions then your engine has big problems. Higher octane prevents that, and so is required for some high performance engines. Those engines designed for lower octane don't get anything out of it but a higher bill.," "It's a measure of stability. Long story short, if your engine doesn't need it (as specified in the owners manual), you'd be wasting money. You actually want the lowest octane fuel your engine can handle, because being the most unstable, it is easiest to yield energy from it. Some engines need higher stability for some technical reasons, but also as a result, those engines are designed to yield more energy out of that fuel; they still want the lowest octane possible. If we can make a stable fuel that can yield more energy per measure, why doesn't every car use it? Because it's expensive to make, and the refining process isn't exact; oil companies can only make so much high octane from crude.," "Certain sporty engines require a higher octane rating. For most cars, 87 is fine. Edit: the manufacturer of your car should let you know which is appropriate for your car. See your owner's manual.

Touchscreen technology employs various methods, notably resistive and capacitive. Resistive screens, once prevalent in older devices like Nintendo products and early smartphones, utilize flexible plastic layers. Pressing the screen forces these layers to compress, creating an electrical connection. Today, capacitive touchscreens—found in most modern smartphones—are far more common. These screens are typically constructed from glass and detect touch through changes in their electric field.  When you touch the screen with your finger, it alters this field, allowing the device to pinpoint the location of the interaction. Non-conductive materials, such as clothing, don’t affect the field and therefore aren’t recognized. “Smartphone gloves” incorporate metallic threads in the fingertips to enable detection. More specifically, capacitive screens function using capacitors – components capable of storing electrical energy between two conductors separated by a dielectric material. Smartphones contain numerous tiny capacitors beneath the screen, and your finger acts as the second conductor, completing the circuit and triggering a response. The device measures the amount of energy stored in each capacitor, determining which ones were touched by a conductive object like your finger.
